hook: The subject here is a former Foundation agent who can no longer perceive other people at all, so nobody can talk to him and he cannot be locked up in any normal way. The entry is short, and much of its weight sits in the addenda. Content note: it touches on despair and a man's attempts to end his own life, handled briefly and without graphic detail.
whyItMatters: It flips the usual arrangement: the anomaly is one of the Foundation's own people, and the staff around him are as much a subject of the file as he is. The addenda read like memos from a supervisor who is angry with colleagues, which says a lot about the site's atmosphere without spelling it out. Containment here is less about walls than about managing what a single person notices.
thingsToNotice: Watch how containment turns into storytelling: the Foundation plants evidence so he will build a narrative that keeps him on site, effectively writing a plot for an audience of one. The incident report shows that the barrier between him and everyone else cuts both ways. Notice, too, how the official tone keeps breaking into reprimands, hinting at behavior the file never fully describes.
